title: Hunters
summary: Mortals who hunt the Kindred: lonely, varied, and driven.

claims.text: Hunters are mortals who hunt vampires; their faces, methods and motives differ, but all seek the destruction of the Kindred.
A hunter knows the vampire only from real encounters, clouded by myth and legend.
Most hunters cannot know how widely the Kindred infest the world, only that something preys on their own home.
The mood is desperate determination.

title: Alone in the Crowd
summary: Why a hunter can expect no thanks and little help.

claims.text: No one hands out medals for killing vampires; even a trusted friend may see the same horror and deny it.
The higher a hunter appeals, the likelier it is to reach someone under vampire influence.
Stockpiling weapons or searching the wrong things online puts a hunter on watch lists, and burning a haven can bring charges of arson or murder.

title: The Big Leagues
summary: The organised hunter societies, seen from the street.

claims.text: Larger, organised hunter groups exist, but a lone hunter may find them bound up in their own protocols.
The Arcanum recruits only those with the right skills and temperament.
The Society of Leopold sends eager amateurs where it lacks the means to go, and prays for any who fall.
Project Twilight agents see civilian hunters as a threat to long operations.

title: The Kindred as Hunters See Them
summary: What a street hunter makes of vampire society.

claims.text: Vampires play at society with politics and sides, and loners are rare but strong.
One side keeps rules about being too obvious and answers to a Prince in each city, meeting in a council.
Its rules cover how much blood may be taken and how many deaths a neighbourhood can bear.
That side would often rather bargain with a hunter than be dragged into the light.
The other side worships its condition like a religion.

title: The Inquisition
summary: The Society of Leopold: the Church's crusaders against the Devil's children.

claims.text: No mortals frighten the Kindred more than the Inquisition.
Its theme is the modern crusader, with the whole world as Holy Land and the Devil as the Enemy.
It recognises four sub-orders (Condotierri, Gladius Dei, the Censor's Office and the Order of Saint Joan); other groups count only as sects.
All its orders aim to deliver humanity from supernatural evil, though their methods differ and even clash.

title: The Arcanum
summary: A scholarly society that studies the supernatural.

claims.text: The Arcanum's charge is knowledge of the otherworldly, and its mandate is knowledge, not war.
Its theme is reckless exploration: members keep going where they know less than they should.
Each Arcanum House funds its Lodges: a small House can keep one, a large House up to five.
Lodges investigate reports of vampires, demons, werewolves and ghosts by interviewing witnesses and scouting.

title: Project Twilight and the SAD
summary: The government hunters.

claims.text: The FBI's Special Affairs Division once hunted monsters with near freedom, and senior figures overlooked its orders for silver bullets and stakes.
Paperwork disguises the work: a raid on a werewolf compound is filed as a strike on terrorists with attack dogs, and silver rounds as Code Five.

title: Numina
summary: The gifts of psychics and hedge magicians.

claims.text: Psychics perceive hidden forces through extrasensory perception and can work on them with their minds.
Some are simply born with talents like telepathy, telekinesis or clairvoyance.
Telekinesis is rated by weight, from one pound at the first level to a thousand pounds at the fifth.

title: Hedge Magic
summary: Folk sorcery of paths and rituals.

claims.text: A hedge magician must hold a world view at odds with modern thinking: a working curse means unlucky thirteens, spilled salt and black cats matter too.

title: True Faith
summary: Divine favour that shields the faithful from the night.

claims.text: True Faith joins deep trust in the divine with divine favour, and only a blessed few have it.
The Faithful can repel vampires and ghosts with a holy symbol or prayer: spend Willpower and roll True Faith against the creature's permanent Willpower; each success is a turn it must flee.
Against a power that targets the Faithful directly and needs a roll, Faith is rolled at difficulty 7 and its successes subtract from the power's.
Powers used passively or indirectly get past that shield.

title: Hunters and Lupines
summary: When hunters cross paths with werewolves.

claims.text: A hunt may stray into werewolf lands, or one threat may menace hunter and werewolf alike.
As allies Lupines are dangerous; as enemies, deadly.

title: Starting Humanity
summary: How a hunter's Humanity begins.

claims.text: A hunter's starting Humanity is Conscience plus Self-Control, a score from 5 to 10, and freebie points can raise it.

title: Hemophiliac
summary: A three-point Physical Flaw.

claims.text: A cut hunter will not stop bleeding without medical help; after lethal or aggravated damage the hunter takes one more bashing level every five minutes until the wound is dressed.
A vampire who bites the hunter can close the wound by licking it, ending the bashing damage.

title: Faith Against Powers
summary: Using True Faith to resist a Discipline.

claims.text: When a Discipline or other power would affect a hunter with True Faith, the player can spend Willpower and roll Faith at difficulty 7; each success takes one from the power's activation roll.
The protection covers only powers aimed directly at the character.

title: Society of Leopold
summary: The modern Inquisition and its orders.

claims.text: The Society, like the Roman Church, is split into smaller divisions that share the aim of freeing humanity from supernatural evil but differ, and sometimes clash, in methods.
It recognises four sub-orders (Order of Saint Joan, Censor's Office, Gladius Dei, Condotierri); every other group is only a sect.
Many Catholic religious orders sit within it; most require vows of poverty, chastity and obedience, and members mark their order with initials after their names.

title: Condotierri
summary: The Society's guard order.

claims.text: Founded in the 15th century, the Condotierri are a quasi-military order that cares more for the Society's safety than for finishing missions, led by a Condotierre-General chosen by the Inquisitor-General.
They guard the larger and older Cenacula and work in lances of three, after the old mounted soldier, squire and lancer.
Novices now train at new combat schools in the Pyrenees and in the Nevada desert; the order is armed like a national military, short of heavy ordnance.
The Society's headquarters is the Monasterio di San Michele in Rome.

title: Gladius Dei
summary: The Sword of God.

claims.text: The Gladius Dei are the Society's elite, called the Sword of God, and its most distinguished order.

title: Ritual of Summoning
summary: A Theurgy rite for calling spirits.

claims.text: The rite lets a Theurgist summon spirits with an extended Charisma + Occult roll at difficulty 9; the successes needed depend on the spirit's power and the Storyteller's call.

title: The Government's Stance
summary: What Washington admits to.

claims.text: Officially the United States Government neither deals with terrorists nor accepts that the supernatural exists.
The FBI will goad suspected terrorists into an attack and then move in at the last moment.

title: Chaoscopes
summary: Devices that track the unnatural.

claims.text: Colonel Riley has trained five chaoscope operators for field work, trailing suspected negative bodies, and one mobile chaoscope has been tested.

title: Forensic Teams
summary: Requisitioned crime-scene help.

claims.text: A forensic team borrowed from a friendly intelligence agency gives results after several weeks; an urgent team processes the scene in six hours and reports in one to two days.

title: The Mob
summary: Organized crime and its vampire masters.

claims.text: Organized crime reaches from drug sales to arms deals, assassinations and swaying governments.
Italian mafia families have been infiltrated and used by vampires more than perhaps any other underworld group, ghouled, enslaved and mind-controlled.

title: Underworld Allies
summary: Allies drawn from crime.

claims.text: For a hunter tied to crime, buying Allies brings hardened members of the underworld rather than law-abiding people.

title: Sense Influence
summary: A three-point Merit.

claims.text: The Merit lets a hunter buy Awareness and sense that someone is under supernatural control or a ghostly presence, with Perception + Awareness at difficulty 8.

title: Ikhwan al-Safa
summary: A hunting order of the Middle East.

claims.text: The Ikhwan al-Safa is named with the Society of Leopold and the Judges as a religious order of vampire hunters.
Its scholars trace it to the Brethren of Sincerity of 10th century Basra, whose teachings survive in the Rasa'il Ikhwan al-Safa, a work of 52 epistles.
Mehmet II is said to have taken most of what that sultan knew of vampires from those epistles.

title: Akritai
summary: Orthodox border guards against the dead.

claims.text: The Akritai descend from a Byzantine military force set to guard the borders; the name comes from the Greek for border.
They keep apart from the other hunting orders, with no fixed hierarchy, only regional groups, mostly in Eastern Europe.
Most are ordained priests or nuns of the Orthodox faith who give up family and goods to destroy vampires.

In 2011 the whole order fought at Domazlice in the Czech Republic and destroyed the seer Tryphosa at heavy cost, finding in the haven a copy of the ancient Book of Nod and a text titled Apostate Auguries, seemingly in the seer's own hand.

title: Knights of St. George
summary: A crusading knighthood.

claims.text: The Resolute Knights of St. George were founded in Syria in the 11th century and by the 1400s had houses from Ireland to India.
The order has long looked forward, taking in women from the 19th century.
